comment: Sends anonymized admin-UI usage telemetry to Magento; turn off if your data-privacy policy forbids outbound tracking.
modal: Beyond opting into usage tracking, this streams anonymized data about how admins use the panel back to Magento/Adobe. Turn it off (No) where your data-privacy policy forbids outbound telemetry. It affects neither the storefront nor store performance.

comment: Scheduled retranslation overwrites manual product-translation edits on the next cron run; can differ per store view.
modal: The native note warns it overwrites manual edits. The mechanism: retranslation runs on a schedule via cron, so any hand-corrected product translation is replaced the next time the job runs. Leave it No if editors maintain translations by hand. Scoped per website/store view.

comment: Only needed if your OpenAI account spans multiple organizations; used only when the OpenAI translation engine is selected.
modal: Set this only if your OpenAI account belongs to more than one organization and requests must be scoped/billed to a specific one; otherwise leave it blank to use your default org. Applies only when the OpenAI translation engine is selected.

comment: Lets themes load templates through symlinks (handy for linked local packages); on production it's an escape-the-theme-dir security risk.
modal: Allowing symlinks lets the template engine follow symlinked paths, convenient when developing with linked packages locally. On production it widens the attack surface: anyone able to place a symlink can make Magento render files outside the theme directory, so keep it No. Scoped per website/store.

comment: Hostname of the SMTP relay Magento hands outgoing mail to; ignored unless the SMTP sending path is in use.
modal: The SMTP server Magento connects to for outgoing mail. As the native note implies, it matters only for the SMTP/Windows sending path; if a transactional-email extension or a different transport handles mail, this value is ignored. Can be set per website/store.

comment: Overrides the admin host/URL; a wrong value can lock you out of admin, and it takes effect only after a cache flush.
modal: Replaces the base URL used for the admin panel (applies only when Use Custom Admin URL is enabled). It must end in a slash and point at a URL that actually serves Magento, since a wrong value locks you out of admin. The change takes effect after the configuration cache is flushed.

comment: Forces visitors onto the canonical base host to avoid duplicate URLs and split sessions; choose off, or a temporary vs permanent redirect.
modal: Redirects requests arriving on a non-canonical host to your configured base URL, preventing duplicate-content and split-session problems. The options let you disable it or pick a temporary versus a permanent redirect; a permanent one is cached hard by browsers and search engines, so test before enabling. Per website/store.

comment: Points secure user/media files at a host or CDN; blank derives it from the secure base URL. Must end in a slash and needs a cache flush.
modal: Sets where secure user media files are served from, e.g. a CDN or separate media host. Leave it empty (or use the {{secure_base_url}}/{{unsecure_base_url}} placeholders) to derive it from the base URL. A missing trailing slash breaks asset paths, and changes apply only after a cache flush. Per website/store.

comment: Chooses which storefront forms show the CAPTCHA; applies only when storefront CAPTCHA is enabled. More forms means more login/checkout friction.
modal: Selects which storefront forms present a CAPTCHA. Applies only when storefront CAPTCHA is enabled, and (per the native note) the Create-user and Forgot-password forms are always protected once chosen. Guarding more forms blocks more bots but adds friction for real users. Scoped per website.

comment: Shortest search term that returns results; must match the search engine's own minimum or results won't line up. Per website/store.
modal: The minimum number of characters a shopper must type before search returns results. As the native note says, it must be consistent with the configured search engine (OpenSearch/Elasticsearch); a mismatch means queries the engine would answer get rejected, or vice-versa. A very low value hurts performance. Per website/store.

comment: Template for auto-building a new product's SKU when left blank; use {{name}} for the product name. Affects only products created afterward.
modal: Pattern used to auto-generate a SKU when a product is saved without one, with {{name}} standing in for the product name. It only shapes SKUs of products created after the change; existing SKUs are untouched.

comment: Initial sort order on category listings before a shopper chooses one; an individual category can override it. Per website/store.
modal: The sort order category pages use by default until a shopper picks another; the options are your available sort attributes. An individual category can override this, and the default can differ per website/store view.

comment: JPEG compression (1-100) for resized images; higher is sharper but larger. Cached images keep old quality until regenerated.
modal: Compression quality applied when Magento resizes or generates JPEGs. Higher values look sharper but produce larger files and slower loads. It affects images generated after the change; already-cached images keep their old quality until the image cache is flushed and regenerated.

comment: Scopes cookies to a URL path; set narrower than / only if the store runs in a subfolder, or logins and cart break. Needs a cache flush.
modal: Restricts the browser to send Magento cookies only under this path. Leave it at / for most stores; narrowing it is right only when the store runs in a subdirectory, otherwise sessions, login and cart silently fail. Takes effect after a cache flush; settable per website/store.

comment: Welcome email for accounts created without a password (admin/API); pick a template with the set-password link. Per website/store.
modal: Used instead of the standard welcome email when an account is created with no password, typically admin- or API-created customers. Choose a template that includes the create-password link so the customer can finish setup; 'Default' resolves via theme fallback. Per website/store.

comment: Minimum characters for customer passwords; raising it affects only new or changed passwords, not existing ones.
modal: Sets the shortest allowed customer password (a number 1 or greater). Increasing it strengthens security but applies only when passwords are created or changed; existing passwords keep working until the customer next resets.

comment: Semicolon-separated values for the name-prefix dropdown (e.g. Mr;Mrs); leave empty to make it a free-text field. Per website.
modal: Defines the choices in the customer name-prefix control. Enter semicolon-separated values (e.g. Mr;Mrs;Dr) to present a dropdown, or leave it blank to let customers type a prefix freely. Scoped per website.

comment: Chooses server- vs client-side style compilation during development; only meaningful outside production mode.
modal: Selects how frontend styles are built during development, server-side compilation versus client-side compilation in the browser. As the native note says, it does nothing in production mode where static assets are pre-deployed; it only shapes the workflow in default/developer mode.

comment: Template for the alert sent when a scheduled currency-rate import fails; applies only when scheduled import is enabled. Per website.
modal: The email template used to notify staff when the scheduled currency-rate import errors out. Applies only when scheduled import is enabled; 'Default' resolves through theme fallback. Scoped per website.

comment: Caps pageSize on GraphQL queries to block expensive requests; applies only when input limits are on. Too low breaks large listings.
modal: Upper bound on how many items a single paginated GraphQL query may request, protecting the server from oversized or expensive calls. Applies only when GraphQL input limits are enabled; setting it below what the storefront asks for will make those queries fail. Per website/store.

comment: Seconds allowed to finish the OAuth handshake before the consumer key/secret expire; shorter is safer but can break slow integrations.
modal: The window, in seconds, in which an OAuth handshake must complete after token exchange begins before the consumer key/secret expire unused. A short window limits how long a leaked key is usable; too short can break integrations that authorize slowly.

comment: Google key used to geocode and measure distances for distance-based source selection; stored encrypted. Needs Geocoding + Distance Matrix APIs.
modal: The Google API key distance-based source selection uses to geocode addresses and compute shipping distances to sources. Per the native note, both the Geocoding and Distance Matrix APIs must be enabled on the key, or source selection cannot rank sources. Stored encrypted.

comment: Lifetime, in minutes, of customer JWT access tokens; shorter is more secure but forces more frequent re-authentication.
modal: How long, in minutes, a customer's JWT access token stays valid. A shorter lifetime limits the damage from a stolen token but makes customers and clients re-authenticate more often; a longer one is more convenient but riskier.

comment: Max height (px) for optimized media-gallery renditions; lower saves storage and bandwidth but reduces detail. Applies to new renditions.
modal: Caps the height, in pixels, of the optimized renditions generated for media-gallery images. Lowering it saves storage and speeds delivery at the cost of detail. It shapes renditions created after the change, not ones already generated.

comment: New Relic API key used to post deployment markers and reporting data; applies only when New Relic reporting is on. Stored encrypted; per website/store.
modal: The New Relic API key Magento uses to post deployment markers and reporting data. Applies only when New Relic reporting is enabled; find it under Events then Deployments in New Relic APM. Stored encrypted and settable per website/store.

comment: Template for the email confirming a newsletter unsubscription; 'Default' resolves via theme fallback. Per website/store.
modal: The email template sent to confirm that someone has unsubscribed from the newsletter. 'Default' resolves through theme fallback. Can differ per website/store view.

comment: Number of columns in new Page Builder column layouts; changing it affects newly added content only, not existing pages.
modal: The default number of columns a new Page Builder column container offers. Raising or lowering it changes the grid for content created afterward; existing pages keep the grid they were built with.

comment: For zero-total orders, whether to auto-invoice the items; when Yes the order goes straight to Processing, skipping manual invoicing. Per website.
modal: For Zero Subtotal Checkout (fully discounted/free) orders, chooses whether Magento auto-invoices all items. As the native note says, Yes places the order directly in Processing and skips the manual invoice step, while No leaves it pending for manual handling. Scoped per website.

comment: Optional language code that forces the reCAPTCHA widget's language; leave blank to auto-detect the visitor's browser language.
modal: Overrides the language the invisible reCAPTCHA widget renders in. Leave it blank to let reCAPTCHA auto-detect from the visitor's browser; set a supported language code only to force a specific language regardless of the visitor.

comment: Toggles collection of storefront report events (viewed/compared products, etc.); disabling stops populating report tables so reports go blank.
modal: Switches on the tracking of report events, such as products viewed, compared, and added to cart. Disabling it (No) stops those events being recorded, so reports and dashboards relying on them show no data for the disabled period. Existing data is not deleted.

comment: Text prepended to generated RMA numbers (e.g. RMA-); identification only, no functional effect. Can differ per website.
modal: A string placed in front of each generated RMA increment ID to make returns easy to recognise. It is purely for identification and does not affect RMA processing. Scoped per website, so separate sites can use distinct prefixes.

comment: Max size (MB) per RMA attachment; also bounded by the server's PHP upload limits. Can differ per website.
modal: Limits the size, in megabytes, of each file a customer attaches to an RMA. The effective ceiling is still capped by the server's PHP upload_max_filesize/post_max_size, so raising this above those has no effect. Scoped per website.

comment: Logo shown on HTML (on-screen) invoice and packing-slip views, not the PDF versions; blank uses the default. Per website/store.
modal: The logo used on the HTML print view of invoices and packing slips, not the PDF documents, which take a separate logo. Accepts jpeg/gif/png; leave it empty to fall back to the default. Settable per website/store so each brand can show its own.

comment: Template for the new-order confirmation email; applies only when order emails are enabled. 'Default' resolves via theme fallback. Per website/store.
modal: The email template used for the order confirmation sent when an order is placed. Applies only when order emails are enabled; 'Default' resolves through theme fallback. Can be set per website/store view.

comment: Comma-separated addresses copied on every invoice email; applies only when invoice emails are on. Useful for an accounting archive. Per website/store.
modal: Extra recipients that receive a copy of every invoice email, entered as comma-separated addresses. Applies only when invoice emails are enabled; handy for routing copies to accounting or an archive mailbox. Settable per website/store.

comment: Template for shipment-comment emails to guest (non-registered) buyers; applies only when shipment emails are enabled. Per website/store.
modal: The email template for shipment-comment notifications sent to guest customers specifically; registered customers use their own template. Applies only when shipment emails are enabled; 'Default' resolves via theme fallback. Per website/store.

comment: When Yes, an email is mandatory when an admin creates an order for a new customer; No lets the order proceed without one. Per website/store.
modal: Controls whether the email field is required when an admin creates an order for a new customer. Yes forces capture of an email (needed for order emails and account linkage); No lets staff place the order without one. Settable per website/store.

comment: Minutes a customer must wait between password-reset requests, to curb abuse; 0 disables the throttle. Applies under a specific reset-protection type.
modal: Throttles how often a customer can request a password reset, limiting reset-flooding abuse; 0 turns the delay off. It takes effect only under the matching Password Reset Protection Type setting. Can be set per website/store.

comment: The <priority> value (0.0-1.0) for category URLs in the XML sitemap; a relative hint to crawlers, not a guarantee. Per website/store.
modal: Sets the <priority> hint (0.0 to 1.0) written for category URLs in the generated XML sitemap, signalling their importance relative to other URLs. Search engines treat it only as a hint, so it influences crawl weighting rather than rankings. Per website/store.

comment: Declares whether entered/gateway shipping amounts already include tax; getting it wrong double-counts or omits shipping tax. Per website.
modal: Tells Magento whether shipping amounts (entered in admin or returned by carriers) already contain tax. If this is set wrong, shipping tax is either double-counted or dropped. Changing it alters how the shipping tax base is computed on new calculations. Scoped per website.

comment: CSS selectors (one per line) whose links are excluded from speculative prerender/prefetch; applies only when speculative loading is on. Per website/store.
modal: Links matching these CSS selectors (one per line) are left out of speculative prerendering/prefetching. Use it to stop prefetching one-shot or state-changing links (logout, add-to-cart, delete) that could fire unintended actions. Applies only when speculative loading is enabled. Per website/store.

comment: How JS string translations are delivered to the browser; changing it requires redeploying static files or storefront JS text breaks.
modal: Chooses the mechanism for delivering JavaScript translations to the storefront (for example a translation dictionary versus embedded strings). As the native note warns, switching strategy requires maintenance mode and a static-content redeploy, or client-side translated text will break.

comment: Browser sessionStorage key under which captured client-side JS errors are stored, so developers can read them from the console.
modal: Names the browser sessionStorage key where the storefront stashes collected JavaScript errors. Developers read that key in the browser console to retrieve the logged errors when debugging client-side issues.

comment: AES/ITN export number for international USPS shipments outside the US; applies only when the USPS REST type is selected. Per website/store.
modal: The Automated Export System / International Transaction Number declared on qualifying international USPS shipments for customs and export compliance. Applies only when the USPS REST API type is selected, and is relevant only for shipments leaving the US. Per website/store.

comment: Max characters in the personal message when a wishlist is shared (255 by default, up to 10000); raising it allows longer notes. Per website/store.
modal: Caps the length of the personal message a customer can add when sharing a wish list, 255 by default and up to 10000. Raising it permits longer notes at some added risk of abuse/spam. Settable per website/store.
